newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates mostly steady amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates mostly steady amid low demand.

text.p: World crude tanker rates were mixed after quiet trading on Wednesday, with many markets feeling the pinch from a supply and demand imbalance, brokers said.
"It's been a pretty bad day," said one broker. "It's as simple as supply and demand - and there just seem to be more ships about than cargo."
Mideast/West rates stood unchanged around W53.5, with Mideast voyages to South Korea at W67 and to Japan at W55.
West Africa routes to the U.S. Gulf were pegged at W87 for a Suezmax and W57.5 for a VLCC. Fixtures east were around Tuesday's levels of W67.5.
Cross Mediterranean charterers faced a different picture with rates still buoyed up by a lack of available ships in the first half of July.
However brokers said the tightness in the market was showing signs of easing off. "Rates haven't changed much, but I think the situation is easing up slightly," said a London broker.
Aframaxes heading cross-Med towards Italy were seen fixed around W120.

Similarly, in the Caribbean brokers reported a moderately tight market as good tonnage availability continued to put pressure on rates. Caribs/U.S. coast rates were assessed between W155-157.5, with one fixture reported at W160.
"It's almost uncomfortably tight," said one broker, "Or comfortably tight depending which side you're on."
Business was relatively quiet in the North Sea. Rates for most routes were unchanged with 80,000 trade rates holding firm around W115-120.
